whatIs.title: What is the Fuel Cost Calculator?
whatIs.description: Estimate trip costs from distance, fuel economy and price, then split fuel, tolls and parking. Includes saved vehicle settings, OPINET regional and historical prices, reimbursement adjustments, reference depreciation, history and a driving log.

howToUse.title: How to Use
items: 1. Enter the distance and choose one way or round trip. Set and save your vehicle type, fuel and fuel economy.
2. Expand fuel prices, region and date to look up OPINET data or enter a price.
3. Add the total tolls and parking. Choose Split costs and enter the number of people. Company reimbursement adjustments remain available.
4. Copy the settlement or share an image/link. Add the trip to your driving log to keep its original amount and settings, view monthly totals and export CSV.

items.q: What vehicle expenses can be claimed as business expenses?
items.a: For corporations and sole proprietors required to keep double-entry books, related costs of a business passenger car (fuel, insurance, repairs, vehicle tax, tolls, depreciation, etc.) are deductible in proportion to the business-use ratio shown in the operation log. Without a log, only up to 15 million KRW of related costs per year is recognized (Corporate Tax Act Enforcement Decree Art. 50-2, Income Tax Act Enforcement Decree Art. 78-3).

items.q: Can I calculate an electric vehicle?
items.a: The fuel list covers gasoline, premium gasoline, diesel and LPG only. For an EV, enter efficiency in km/kWh as the custom efficiency and the charging price (KRW/kWh) as the fuel price; the same formula (distance ÷ efficiency × price) applies.

Business passenger cars are depreciated straight-line over 5 years, and depreciation above 8 million KRW per year in the business-use amount is carried forward (Corporate Tax Act Enforcement Decree Art. 50-2). Vehicles that are not business passenger cars, such as light cars, vans with 9+ seats and trucks, follow the general depreciation rules. The per-km depreciation in this calculator is a reference value by vehicle class, not the tax depreciation amount.

tips.title: Tips
items: Keep a detailed mileage log for business vehicles to maximize tax deductions.
Use the real-time fuel price refresh feature for accurate current-rate calculations.
The depreciation coefficient (×1.0–1.5) is a company-policy multiplier applied to the fuel cost. If your company reimburses wear on personal cars by marking up fuel cost, enter that multiplier.
Compare regional fuel prices to improve the accuracy of business trip expense reports.
